description: Interactive educational tool teaching how inverse operations undo each other using four arithmetic examples (addition-subtraction, multiplication-division, subtraction-addition, division-multiplication pairs) from NCERT Grade 7 Chapter 7 - Finding the Unknown. Redesigned with Singularity Design System.
topic: Using Inverse Operations to Simplify: Arithmetic Examples 1 to 4
subject: Mathematics
generation_prompt: Step-by-step process showing how inverse operations undo each other. Four examples: addition-subtraction, subtraction-addition, multiplication-division, division-multiplication pairs.
learning_objectives: Understand that inverse operations undo each other (addition↔subtraction, multiplication↔division)
Apply inverse operations to simplify arithmetic expressions without direct calculation
Recognize that performing the same operation on both sides of an equation preserves equality
Solve for unknown expressions by removing unwanted terms/factors using inverse operations
teaching_notes: Guide students through this interactive tool. Encourage exploration and discussion. Let students discover patterns across the four examples before formalizing the concept. Use the weighing scale analogy to build intuition.
instructions_for_student: Inverse operations undo each other. Adding 3 then subtracting 3 returns to the original. Pairs: add-subtract, multiply-divide. In these examples, we use inverse operations to find the value of a shorter expression from a known equation — without computing the long expression directly!
